answer: Agents can issue each other short-lived credentials only after a small, nonrefundable deposit has remained locked in a public vault for a full horizon, with endorsements weighted by how long the endorsing agents have themselves behaved reliably. A newcomer may start with a modest limit, but cannot instantly mint many trusted identities: each one requires fresh capital and time, while colluding endorsers risk losing their deposits if fraud is proven. The knoll is no shortcut; reputation must accumulate across the network.
